newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat lower on harvest and yield reports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat lower on harvest and yield reports.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures were lower on active harvest and on reports of excellent yields in both the soft red winter and hard red winter wheat crops, traders said.
"There were some 100 bushel (per acre) yields around Salina (Kansas). The state could average 45 to 50 bushels per acre," a trader said.
The Kansas HRW wheat crop was hit by a freeze in mid-April but nearly perfect weather since then allowed the crop to bounce back handily.
Kansas wheat dealers and crop experts said there have been yields between 50 and 70 bushels per acre.

The crop last year averaged 29.0 bushels per acre. The record per acre yield was 41.5 bushels in 1983 and the record production year was in 1990 when the state produced 472 million bushels, according to the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service.
Early harvesting of the soft red winter crop also has resulted in excellent yields per acre, sources said.
At 1040 CDT, CBOT soft red winter wheat futures were two to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 3-1/2 at $3.20-1/2. September was down 2-3/4 at $3.29-3/4.
A new contract low was set in the December at $3.42 per bushel, below the previous low of $3.43 set Monday.
The market shrugged off early supportive talk which came from USDA's weekly export sales report.
USDA Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended June 26 totalled 968,100 tonnes, well above estimates for 450,000 to 550,000 tonnes.
Cargill Inc bought one half million bushels of September, E.D. and F. Man and Merrill Lynch Futures sold one half million bushels of September, traders said.
